We have applied 20810 to target, got two fragments: "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1" and "O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F". That's product of disconnection: target -> these two precursors.

Now we need to apply next template 2895 to the first fragment (maybe). The result gave nitrated aromatic? Actually applied 2895 to that fragment gave "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1". So it introduced nitro group? The template likely converts an aniline to nitro? Actually 2895 seems to convert an aniline to nitro? The forward reaction is nitro to aniline? The retro template would break nitro to aniline? Anyway we have product with nitro group.

Now we need to continue applying templates 1914397, 1914398, 1914399, 74054 in order. Likely each will act on subsequent fragments.

We need to generate a JSON route tree with each reaction node having children (precursors). The root is target molecule. Reaction 1 uses template 20810, children are two molecules (precursor A and B). Then for each precursor we may apply further reactions sequentially, ensuring total at least 6 reactions. The order must be as given, but can be applied to appropriate molecules.

Thus:

Step1 (template 20810) on target -> gives prec1 = "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1" (call A) and prec2 = "O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F" (call B).

Step2 (template 2895) on A -> gives A2 = "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1". (B unchanged)

Step3 (template 1914397) likely acts on A2 to break nitro? Let's apply to A2.
